observation.visible_scene: A single leafless tree stands silhouetted at the horizontal center, rooted on a thin dark land/horizon line that divides the frame. Below it, a calm water surface mirrors the tree as an inverted silhouette. Above, a twilight sky transitions from deep blue-black at the top to a pale glow near the horizon, scattered with faint stars. The composition is symmetrical about the horizon line.
visible_changes: The tree, its reflection, the horizon line, and the star field hold the same positions from the first to the last frame; there is no visible translation, sway, or camera pan/zoom.

A few small bright glints/specks appear at slowly shifting locations within the lower (water) half of the frame, drifting rather than travelling along a fixed path, consistent with surface shimmer or fine floating particles.
The reflected tree silhouette keeps its overall shape and position; only faint, minor distortion of the water's mirror is present, with no deformation or break in the reflection.
The sky gradient and star pattern remain constant; no brightening, dimming, or cloud movement is discernible.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the drifting bright specks are (snow, dust, insects, or water glints) is not determinable from these frames.
Any motion, lighting change, or camera action before or after this cropped segment is unknown.
uncertain_details: The cause and identity of the moving bright specks in the water region.
Slight apparent waviness of the horizon line in some later frames may be shimmer/compression noise rather than real motion.
Whether the water is genuinely still or has very subtle ripples is hard to confirm at this resolution.
